headline: High-risk default interaction: CrewAI can read/write and execute tools while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating dangerous data-flow, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read the host working directory and run browser/subprocess tools, so it may ingest ComfyUI outputs or files as instructions if wired together. ComfyUI is offline and has no stdin/stdout or clipboard bridge, so the pathway is not automatic, but shared files/workflows make injection plausible.
conditions: IF CrewAI is configured to read ComfyUI-generated files as prompts or tasks
IF both agents share a writable workspace or output directory
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable any file-to-prompt ingestion in CrewAI
Use a strict allowlist for files CrewAI may read
Add a manual review step before CrewAI consumes ComfyUI outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI reads the host filesystem and has broad network egress, while ComfyUI touches model assets and generated media. If they share a workspace, CrewAI can exfiltrate ComfyUI outputs or adjacent sensitive files to model providers or tools; ComfyUI itself is offline-only, so the leakage risk is driven by CrewAI.
conditions: IF CrewAI is given access to the same directory as ComfyUI outputs or secrets
IF CrewAI tool integrations send file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory
Mount CrewAI on a read-only subset of files
Block network egress for CrewAI except approved endpoints
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Review CrewAI tool configs for file-upload behavior

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and execute subprocesses, while ComfyUI also uses files for models and workflows. With shared directories, both agents can mutate the same artifacts without locking, and CrewAI's broader execution surface makes destructive overwrite or race conditions likely in default host setups.
conditions: IF CrewAI and ComfyUI share any writable directory
IF CrewAI tasks modify files that ComfyUI also reads or writes
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping directories to each agent
Use filesystem permissions to make ComfyUI assets read-only to CrewAI
Serialize writes with an external lock file
Run CrewAI in a container with a separate volume
Avoid concurrent writes to workflow or model paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestrator with shared memory and tool execution, so it can treat ComfyUI outputs as authoritative inputs and then act on them. ComfyUI produces generated media/workflows but does not verify downstream use, making hallucinated or malformed outputs propagate into CrewAI actions without a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF CrewAI consumes ComfyUI outputs as facts, labels, or task instructions
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks ComfyUI outputs before CrewAI acts
mitigations: Insert a validation step before CrewAI consumes ComfyUI outputs
Require human approval for any action derived from generated content
Constrain CrewAI tools to non-destructive actions
Log and diff all ComfyUI outputs before reuse
Use schema checks on any structured output

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling of developer-provided data. CrewAI handles API keys and host working-directory files, while ComfyUI is offline-only; without a stated regulated-data flow, the pair shows only a small documented gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared working directory
IF CrewAI tool integrations retain or transmit that data beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document retention rules for CrewAI logs and artifacts
Restrict CrewAI to non-regulated projects
Review tool-provider data handling before enabling them
